question: What will the first reported revenues after September 2026 be for the following companies? (Nvidia)

calls.reasoning: Nvidia guided Q3 FY27 revenue to $108.0B +/-2% (Aug 26, 2026 8-K), with no China data center compute assumed. Over the last ~8 quarters it beat midpoint guidance by about 2.5-8% (median ~5%): Q2 FY27 $96.2B vs $91B guide (+5.7%), Q1 FY27 $81.6B vs ~$78B (+4.6%, guide not confirmed), Q3 FY26 $57.0B vs $54B (+5.6%). Applying that to $108B gives a center near $113B. The analyst consensus is $108.8-111.4B and the highest LSEG estimate is $112.2B. Market check: I found no total-revenue market on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold. Polymarket has a thin (~$2k), internally inconsistent Q3 data center revenue market whose prices imply total revenue near $113B; I used it as weak evidence only. Upside tail: a beat above ~7.5% or China revenue resuming.

calls.reconciliation: The three runs agree on the guidance ($108.0B +/-2%), the Q2 FY27 actual ($96.2B vs $91B) and a history of beating the midpoint by 2.5-7.9%. They differ only on small points. (1) The Q1 FY27 guide of $78B is unverified in Run 1 and cited as a company release in Run 2. It changes the mean beat by less than 0.3pp, so it doesn't matter. (2) Consensus figures range from $104.2B (at the time of the guide) to $108.8-111.4B (later). Those differences come from timing, and consensus usually sits below what the history of beats implies, so I give it little weight. (3) The market evidence differs: Run 1 found a Polymarket data-center market and Run 3 found none. Either way the markets are thin, mismatched contracts, so they are not anchors. (4) The upper-tail mass ranges from 8% to 12%, which is a judgment call. A normal distribution on the beat (mean about 5%, SD about 1.7pp) gives roughly 8-10% for a beat above 7.4%, so I took 9%. I carried forward the runs' shared reference class. No web access was available on this run.
